subject: Sable Retail: Surge of 429/504s During Peak Checkout — Networking Investigation & Exec Escalation
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@sable-retail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 07:55:00 -0700
Subject: High 429/504 errors during morning peak

Neha,

We started seeing a big spike in 429 and 504 responses from Redwood during our 07:30–08:15 PST checkout surge. Customers are reporting failed payments and timeouts — checkout conversion down ~12% in the last 30 minutes. Our engineers are seeing retry storms on outbound calls to your endpoint and large tail latencies (p50 fine, p95/p99 blown out).

Can you confirm if anything changed on the Redwood side or if there are known networking issues? We've attached short client-side logs and a dashboard snapshot. This is causing an immediate revenue impact for us.

Attachments: sable_client_errors.txt (snippet), checkout-spike.png

— Amit Shah
Head of Engineering, Sable Retail
amit@sable-retail.com

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 429/504 errors during morning peak

Amit —

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m escalating immediately to our SRE and network teams (cc’d). I apologize for the disruption — we know checkout availability is critical.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you forward a short pcap/flow sample or VPC egress logs if available?
- If you can share timestamps for a couple of failed request IDs that helps correlation.

Jordan/Laura/Karthik — please triage network path and NAT/peering immediately. Priorities: verify VPC peering health, NAT connection pool saturation, any firewall state drops, and DNS latency anomalies. If you confirm a customer-facing incident, please open an incident channel and loop in Ops.

I’ll coordinate with Amit and will prepare an exec note once we have root cause or a mitigation.

— Neha

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 429/504 errors during morning peak

Amit / Neha — quick triage notes from the application side:
- We see a correlated spike of 429s emitted by our gateway at ~07:31 PST, followed by increased 504s as retries saturated upstream capacity.
- Token queuing metrics show sudden backlog in the dedicated pool servicing Sable (token_avail dropped to near-zero for ~3m).
- No deploys on our hosted control plane in that time window.

I'm running checks against:
- VPC peering status between Sable's VPC and our Dedicated nodes (API call + flow logs)
- NAT table metrics — looking for ephemeral port exhaustion or 1:1 mapping churn
- Firewall stateful connection counts on the edge nodes

I'll share logs and a short timeline in the incident channel. If this is NAT ephemeral port exhaustion or peering retransmits we should mitigate with temporary burst capacity and redirect routing to an alternate region.

— Jordan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@sable-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 429/504 errors during morning peak

Amit/Team — quick summary of findings so far (logs attached):
- We see repeated TCP retransmits and SYN retransmits from the path between our Dedicated egress nodes and Sable’s peered VPC: packet drops peaked ~07:30–07:40 PST.
- NAT ephemeral port usage spiked; our NAT pool allocation shows short-lived port exhaustion on a handful of nodes. Likely cause: concurrent client retries amplified by our admission controls leading to queue buildup and 429s.
- No kernel-level firewall policy changes during that window; however, an intermediate customer-side firewall appliance reported state table pruning at ~07:33 (we've got their log reference).

Immediate mitigations applied at 08:50 PST:
- Opened temporary extra NAT capacity on the affected Dedicated pool (increased ephemeral port range on 3 hosts).
- Enabled smart backoff rule for the Sable route to reduce retry amplification (rate-limit at the edge for retries, preserve successful traffic).
- Failed request sampling enabled and a short debug capture started; attaching a sanitized capture and the internal runbook we followed.

Next steps:
- Recommend Sable engineering review firewall appliance state table / connection timeouts; the appliance appears to be pruning established connections which triggers reconnect storms.
- Plan: schedule a coordinated rekey/connection drain outside of peak tomorrow and add longer-lived TCP keepalives; we'll run a controlled load test beforehand.

Attachments: dashboard-429-spike.png, sable_flow_capture.pcap (sanitized), runbook-network-triage.pdf

— Laura Bennett
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai

From: Amit Shah <amit@sable-retail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 429/504 errors during morning peak

Thanks — this is very helpful. Our infra team confirms the firewall/appliance was under high state churn and trimmed older entries to reclaim memory during the spike. They're going to increase the state table size and adjust TCP timeouts. We are also going to enable connection reuse on our side for the checkout workers.

A couple of asks for exec reporting:
- Can Redwood provide a short RCA and timeline and any credit offer for the minute-level revenue hit?
- Can you confirm if this could recur if we see a heavier-than-normal retry amplification tomorrow morning?

I'll keep you posted; appreciate the fast response.

— Amit
Head of Engineering, Sable Retail
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@sable-retail.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 429/504 errors during morning peak — Exec note

Amit / Neha / Team —

Thank you for the quick coordination. High level summary for Sable execs:
- Incident window: 07:30–08:20 PST (root cause window ~07:31–07:40 PST).
- Symptom: elevated 429s then 504s caused by retry amplification combined with intermediate firewall state table pruning and ephemeral port exhaustion on our Dedicated egress nodes.
- Immediate mitigation: temporary expansion of NAT ephemeral range + edge retry-rate smoothing (completed by 08:50 PST).
- Customer impact: transient checkout failures; Sable reported ~12% checkout conversion impact for the peak 30-minute window.

Planned next steps (owners):
- Redwood SRE (Laura): follow-up RCA doc with packet captures and timeline (ETA EOD today).
- Redwood Product/Infra (Karthik/Jordan): implement a persistent mitigation: increase NAT pool margins for Dedicated pools by default for high-throughput customers and add an automated detection for retry storms.
- Customer (Amit): extend firewall state table and enable connection reuse; coordinate on a non-peak drain test tomorrow.
- Commercial: Neha to propose a goodwill credit for Sable’s impacted window; recommend a 1-time credit and a review of the Dedicated sizing for Q3.

We take outages like this seriously — Neha, please propose a short credit and I'll review. Laura, please upload the RCA to the HubSpot ticket and attach the sanitized captures.

— Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai
